title: The AI Autocrat
gist: Seva Gunitsky and Bruce Schneier open their essay on how AI both empowers and imperils dictators with Russia: after Channel One editor Marina Ovsyannikova's March 2022 on-air anti-war protest, no one has protested on Russian TV since, partly due to tighter security and fear, though propagandist Margarita Simonyan offered another explanation in October 2024. Only the opening is available (teaser).

insights.claim: Two weeks after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Channel One editor Marina Ovsyannikova held up a sign on the evening newscast reading 'Stop the war. Don't believe propaganda. They're lying to you!' before being dragged away.
insights.speaker: Seva Gunitsky
insights.so_what: Illustrates the human vulnerability in autocratic propaganda systems that technology might be used to eliminate.
insights.quote: Stop the war. Don’t believe propaganda. They’re lying to you!
insights.locator: Two weeks after Moscow’s full-scale invasion

insights.claim: No one has protested the war on Russian television since Ovsyannikova, partly because of tighter security and a general climate of fear; in October 2024 chief propagandist Margarita Simonyan offered another explanation.
insights.speaker: Seva Gunitsky
insights.so_what: Autocratic information control in Russia has tightened, reducing the chance of internal dissent disrupting state narratives.
insights.locator: No one has protested the war

themes.theme: AI as a tool and threat for autocrats

insights.claim: The authors argue that AI technology both empowers and imperils dictators.
insights.speaker: Seva Gunitsky
insights.so_what: AI's political effects cut both ways — strengthening surveillance and propaganda while creating new vulnerabilities for authoritarian regimes.

insights.claim: AI surveillance technology is being demonstrated in the United States, as in Phoenix, Arizona in May 2026, signalling the tools under discussion are not confined to autocracies.
insights.speaker: Seva Gunitsky
insights.so_what: Growth of AI surveillance markets in democracies raises regulatory and civil-liberties risk for vendors.
insights.quote: A demonstration of AI surveillance technology, Phoenix, Arizona, May 2026
